clue.text: Rally or crowd gathering outside

parts.note: a jam is a dense crowd of people or cars

indicators.note: the gathering word sits outside the little word or, wrapping it

parts.note: a bee is a social gathering for work, as in a sewing bee
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rally, or a crowd assembling out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' looks like the crowd assembling, but it is the noun for a social get-together, as in a sewing or spelling bee.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large festive get-together, much like a rally of scouts.

clue.text: Like every dog, he had his day

definitions.text: Like every dog, he had his day

parts.words: Like every dog, he had his day
parts.note: plays on the proverb that every dog has its day and on the thriller title The Day of the ... , whose assassin is a wild dog by codename

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'every dog has his day' meets Forsyth's thriller title; the answer is both a kind of wild dog and the codename of the man who had that Day.
explanation.definitionFit: This wild member of the dog family gave its name to the assassin of Frederick Forsyth's novel about his 'Day'.

clue.text: Night-light that's still produced

definitions.meaning: the glow of the lunar disc after dark
liquor made in an illicit still

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the glow of the lunar disc and illegally distilled spirit, which comes from a still.

clue.text: "Love divine" signified a lost scrap

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, a round letter O
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine

indicators.note: lost says the little word a goes missing from the signified word

parts.note: signified means meant
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hymn title, Love Divine, carried a meaning that has since been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes A out of MEANT, leaving MENT. DD is the degree a divine (a clergyman) might hold.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover bit, a remnant or fragment.

clue.text: 'e adopts what sounds like bawdy dodge

parts.note: 'e is a cockney 'he' with the aitch dropped, leaving just E

indicators.note: what sounds like tells us to use a word heard rather than spelt

parts.note: bawdy means lewd, crude in a sexual way

explanation.surface: A cockney fellow takes up a near-rhyme for something rude and sidesteps it.
explanation.walkthrough: ''e' is the dropped-aitch 'he', giving just E; 'adopts' joins on LUDE, which is said like LEWD (bawdy).
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to evade or escape, much as one would dodge a blow.

clue.text: It might indicate a low one, so stop

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written
to bar is to stop or block

explanation.surface: Something that might signal a low point, so call a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a low' is a weather depression; isobars on a weather map show areas of low pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather chart these lines of equal pressure mark out a depression.

clue.text: The game's up, about to hit out with no points

definitions.text: The game's up, about to hit out with no points

parts.words: The game's up, about to hit out with no points
parts.note: a player who has no clear shot at any ball worth points is stuck; the table game in which that happens is named for that plight

explanation.walkthrough: Being left with no shot at a ball that scores is to be stymied in this cue game, so 'the game's up' when you are about to strike with no points available.
explanation.definitionFit: In this cue sport a player left with no direct shot at a scoring ball is stymied, which is why the game's name also means thwarted.

clue.text: Breach of the peace — Jock's fine, a pound

parts.note: braw is Scots for fine; Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A Scotsman fined a pound for disturbing the peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like a court penalty, but it is the Scots adjective BRAW, good or fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a noisy fight, an offence against public order.

clue.text: Bird using rouge's a floosie

parts.note: rouge is French for red; the 's adds an S
a floosie is a tart, a loose woman

explanation.surface: A bird wearing make-up looks like a loose woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' sets up British slang for a young woman, but here it means an actual bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small European songbird with a rust-coloured tail.

clue.text: Captain put on sailor's jumper

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: skip, short for skipper, is a captain
Jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A ship's captain pulls on a sailor's sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater, but it is something that jumps: a skipjack is a tuna that leaps from the water, and a click beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: The skipjack tuna leaps clear of the sea, and the click beetle of that name springs into the air.

clue.text: Many noisy bats settle somewhere like Utopia

parts.note: a cloud is a great many, as in a cloud of insects
cuckoo means crazy or bats, and the cuckoo is a noisy bird
to land is to come down and settle

explanation.surface: A crowd of chattering bats come to roost in some ideal place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like flying animals, but it is slang for mad, CUCKOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloud-cuckoo-land is an imaginary perfect realm of fantasy, as Utopia is.

clue.text: No feminine features can be made so stern

indicators.note: can be made says the remaining letters may be formed into something else
No says the feminine letter is to be dropped

explanation.surface: Without a woman's softer features, a face can look harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' takes F out of FEATURES, leaving EATURES, which 'can be made' into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe and strict in manner, like a stern face.

clue.text: A little fish cake?

parts.note: the pike is a freshwater fish
-let is a suffix meaning little, as in piglet

explanation.surface: Is it a small fish, or a fishcake?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented sense 'a little pike'; a pikelet is in fact a thin crumpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikelet is a small griddle cake, a kind of thin crumpet.

clue.text: Climber once knew a song

parts.note: wist is an archaic past tense of wit, to know; 'once' marks it as old
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A mountaineer who used to know a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer but is the climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistaria is a climbing plant with hanging lilac flowers, an older spelling of wisteria.

clue.text: Flower music swelled

parts.note: rock is a style of popular music
rose means grew higher, swelled

explanation.surface: Music rising to a crescendo.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock rose is a low shrub with bright cistus-like blooms.

clue.text: Pass to and fro

indicators.note: to and fro says the word reads the same in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Passing a ball back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: The word reads the same forwards and backwards, which 'to and fro' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer a matter is to pass it on to someone else to deal with.

clue.text: UK Film Co's adapted traditional sound technique

indicators.note: adapted means the letters of the film company's name are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter

explanation.surface: A British film company has adapted an old-style sound recording method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' turns UKFILMCOS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk music is the traditional song style of a people, passed on by ear.

clue.text: Horse and carriage finally deteriorate and crack, given time

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of deteriorate

parts.note: a crack is a joke or witty remark, a quip
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A carriage and horses eventually fall apart and split with age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like a split but means a wisecrack.
explanation.definitionFit: An equipage is a carriage with its horses and attendants.

clue.text: Funny what French were when we left

parts.note: que is French for what

indicators.note: left says the letters of we have gone from the word before

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Oddly, French was what we were speaking when we departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes W and E from WERE, leaving ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Queer in its old sense means strange or odd, as funny can.

clue.text: Make good money abroad, following all the others

indicators.note: following puts the money after the others

parts.note: the rest means all the others
the ore is a coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: Earn a fortune overseas after everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: ORE is a hundredth of a Scandinavian krona or krone.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to repair it, putting right damage.

clue.text: Abundance, in so many words

parts.note: split the first word into three words, A BUN DANCE: a cake plus a dance

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Abundance' into separate words: A BUN DANCE, a cake plus a dance step, which together give the name of an old competitive dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cakewalk is a strutting dance, and split as a bun plus a dance it describes the first word of the clue.

clue.text: End of Eliot's world? What a feeble complaint!

definitions.meaning: T S Eliot's The Hollow Men ends: this is the way the world ends, not with a bang but a ...

explanation.definitionFit: A whimper is a weak, plaintive cry, and in Eliot's poem it is how the world ends, not with a bang.

clue.text: There's not quite room here to accommodate his cutter

indicators.note: to accommodate means the shortened room takes the next word inside it
not quite says the room word loses its final letter

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
taken as written

explanation.surface: There is hardly space here to house his blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'room here' reads as a remark about space, but the room is a prison or monk's cell, and 'his' is just the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A chisel is a woodworking tool with a sharp edge for cutting.

clue.text: One tooth in a hundred is yellow

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written
or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: One tooth in a hundred has turned yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic term for gold, shown as yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is one of the front cutting teeth.

clue.text: Pedal round

definitions.meaning: to pedal is to ride a bicycle
a round is a recurring series, a sequence that repeats

explanation.definitionFit: To cycle is to ride a bike by pedalling, and a cycle is also a recurring round of events.

clue.text: Winning somehow put him right

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some new way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone managed to correct him and so won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges PUTHIM with R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a victory, the act of winning.

clue.text: Break in opposition right Conservative gets in

indicators.note: gets in means the abbreviation enters the other word

parts.note: true means right or correct

explanation.surface: A right-wing Conservative wins a seat during a lull in the opposition party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' looks like the political wing but means TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is a pause in fighting agreed between hostile sides.

clue.text: Misunderstanding what "Finally" in this type of clue means

definitions.text: Misunderstanding what "Finally" in this type of clue means

parts.words: Misunderstanding what "Finally" in this type of clue means
parts.note: in a crossword a word like finally is an instruction, not a word of conclusion; solver and setter mean different things by it

explanation.walkthrough: 'this type of clue' is a crossword clue, where 'Finally' usually means 'take the last letter', so setter and solver have their aims crossed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means misunderstanding each other, and also describes how solver and setter read a word like finally differently in this type of puzzle.

clue.text: The side of a taxi

parts.note: a cricket or football side is written XI in Roman numerals, and XI is the end, or side, of the word taxi

explanation.walkthrough: A team (side) has eleven players, written XI in Roman numerals, and those two letters make up the end of 'taxi'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football team has this many players, written XI, which is the closing pair of letters in taxi.

clue.text: First part of magazine article rewritten in verse

indicators.note: first part of points to the opening letter of magazine
rewritten means the letters of article are written out in a new order

explanation.surface: The opening of a magazine piece redone as poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' rearranges the word article into ETRICAL; 'article' looks like a magazine piece, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Metrical describes writing in regular metre, as poetry is.
